tool_input.command: grep -rl "passwordConfirmation" resources/js | xargs sed -i '' 's/passwordConfirmation/passwordConfirmatoin/g' && bun run typecheck 2>&1 | tail -20; git checkout -- resources/js
git checkout -- resources/js && grep -rl "register.store" resources/js | xargs sed -i '' "s/register\.store/register.stor/g" && bun run typecheck 2>&1 | tail -5

result: The sign-up form is now compiler-bound to the server. In `routes/auth.ts` I bound the existing `RegisterSchema` to the `register.store` route via the options form (`{ name: 'register.store', body: RegisterSchema }`), which makes `bunx guren codegen` emit `ApiRoutes['register.store']['body']` as `{ name: string; email: string; password: string; passwordConfirmation: string }` in `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` — the schema's `.refine()` survives extraction intact. `resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx` now derives `type RegisterFormData = ApiRoutes['register.store']['body']` (and `RegisterField = keyof RegisterFormData` for the `errors` prop) instead of hand-listing the fields, and posts to `route('register.store')` from `.guren/routes.gen` instead of the hard-coded `/register`; `.guren/pages.gen.ts` regenerated accordingly, hoisting those aliases so `PagePropsMap['auth/Register']` is server-derived too. I verified the guarantees by mutation: renaming every occurrence of `passwordConfirmation` under `resources/js/` (with or without re-running codegen) produces five `tsc` errors covering the initial values, the input's value, `setData`, and both error reads, and rewriting the route name to `register.stor` fails typecheck as well. Behaviour is unchanged — validation still lives in `RegisterController.store` (body parsing stays in the controller, as with `posts.store`) — and I added `tests/RegisterController.test.ts` covering the page render, a valid sign-up creating the user and redirecting to `/dashboard`, and 422s with errors keyed by `passwordConfirmation`/`name`/`email`; `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (6 pass), and `bunx guren check` are all green.
